eval.title: CNH Industrial Stock Analysis - Deep Dive NYSE: CNH

call.headline_quote: likely to give a 10 11% long-term return at the moment there are dividends buyback there is the food cycle food sector long-term growth

scenarios.name: normal
scenarios.quote: if we put a growth rate across a cycle of 5% a discount rate of 10% a terminal multiple of 15 on earnings per share dividend payout ratio 35% so there is some income there the intrinsic value is $113

reasons.claim: The business is deep in a cyclical downturn with revenues, earnings and margins all down sharply, and the decline is expected to continue into 2025.
reasons.quote: Consolidated revenues down 28% which is staggering for any business but usually not that uncommon in a cyclical food agricultural business consequently ebit is down 71% net income 70%

data_check.gap_note: he says 0.28, as-of 0.0482357 (FY2023); annual vs TTM or a different definition; not in our data: ebit decline, net income decline

reasons.claim: At the current price the stock offers an 11% long-term return, and in a worse 2025 downturn it could be bought at a stronger cyclical return of up to 20%.
reasons.quote: it is is now leading to an 11% long-term return however with cyclicals you can sometimes buy them at 20% not just 10%

data_check.gap_note: not in our data: expected return, cyclical buy return

reasons.claim: The company returns significant cash to shareholders via dividends and buybacks and plans to continue, though the dividend will likely decline with lower earnings.
reasons.quote: in 2024 they returned approximately 1.3 billion to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases

data_check.gap_note: he says 0.3, as-of 0.226908 (FY2023); annual vs TTM or a different definition; not in our data: shareholder returns

reasons.claim: Financial services delinquencies could rise if food prices fall further, hurting farmer profitability and creating additional risk on top of the equipment cycle.
reasons.quote: food prices are still likely at the profitable level for Farmers but you never know if food prices go lower then it can be unprofitable for I don't know farmers

reasons.claim: Tariff uncertainty and a volatile political environment make it hard for the company and farmers to plan investment, weighing on near-term demand.
reasons.quote: this is very volatile environment and hard to make business decisions in a such a volatile environment

external_facts_used: David Einhorn's public comment that CNH is a good long-term buy offering 10+ earnings yields and growth
Company guidance on 2025 industry unit declines (Global -5 to -10%, North America -10 to -15%)
Management's $600 million annual run-rate cost savings target
Company's stated dividend policy of 25-35% (later stated 30-50%) of prior-year net income
Company relocating some production to the US would take 18-20 months due to tariff uncertainty
IPO/demerger history: CNH went public 12 years ago at $112, demerged from Iveco in 2022
Deere's reported P/E of ~30 and declining guidance despite stock strength

critic.notes: ok — he calls it a fair business at ~10-11% return, places it with higher cyclical risk on the quadrant, and personally keeps watching (maybe a small position); a strong buy only at 15%+ cycle returns.
